generated_note: v2.2.0: precision hardening patch. Added risk-floor mechanism so that specific, pre-defined strong evidence combinations (credential theft+C2, keylogging+C2, injection+recon, security tampering+destruction, 3+ independent injection primitives) can never be scored as SAFE regardless of numeric score. A single API or string still never triggers MALICIOUS on its own. Combination rules now support two forms: requires_categories (cross-category) and requires_multiple_in_category (in-category multiplicity, new in 2.2.0). See engine.js changelog for the rest of the hardening pass.

combination_rules.name: multiple_independent_injection_primitives
combination_rules.description: Three or more independent process-injection primitives (e.g. remote memory allocation + remote memory write + remote thread creation) were found together. A single such API is common in legitimate low-level tooling; three or more acting in concert is a much stronger signal of actual injection capability being assembled, not incidental API use.

ordinal_import_heuristic.description: A high proportion of imports resolved purely by ordinal (no function name) can indicate deliberate evasion of static name-based scanning, but many legitimate DLLs (e.g. MFC, some MSVC runtime helpers) also use a handful of ordinal imports. This is treated as weak, contextual evidence only.

extension_mismatch_heuristic.description: The file was uploaded with a .dll/.asi extension, but the PE COFF Characteristics field does not have IMAGE_FILE_DLL set. This can indicate an executable (.exe) renamed to look like a GTA plugin. This is metadata evidence, not proof of malice — some legitimate loader stubs are also built as EXEs.

timestamp_anomaly_heuristic.description: The PE COFF TimeDateStamp is either zero, implausibly old (before the year 1993, predating Win32 PE itself), or in the future relative to the scan time. Timestamps are trivially forgeable and this is purely informational metadata.
